values: Every senior retiree who leaves the organization takes with them 30 years of living memory: error patterns, failed solutions, optimal paths, and tacit knowledge not recorded in any system. Retirement centers today are warehouses of this treasure, but have no mechanism to extract, store, and distribute that knowledge.
Cost of this forgetfulness: repetition of the same mistakes in the parent organization, inefficient services in the center, and waste of human capital that could be a problem-solving resource.

The retiree community is not homogeneous. From those unable to even follow up on a letter to those who can analyze others' cases. From those who only want to observe to those who want to make demands. From those who are a resource in a crisis to those who are the target.
But the current system (or lack thereof) treats everyone the same. Result: the needy are abandoned, the capable remain idle, the claimant becomes frustrated, and collective intelligence is wasted.

In normal times, the center is a welfare-information entity. But in a crisis (war, earthquake, pandemic, total internet blackout), the center could become a distributed relief headquarters. With 30 years of experience among retirees, without needing new training – only intelligent coordination.
Today's reality: This capability does not exist. In the next crisis, the center will shift from being part of the solution to part of the problem.
If these three crises are not resolved, retirement centers will gradually become ineffective, passive, value-less institutions. This plan is a response to all three crises.
